title: I wanted a game like Valheim on my phone. 2 Months later it's on Google Play
author: nospoon99
selftext:
Showcasing some gameplay for my game, Samonios, and a few details that others might find helpful.

TL;DR: solo dev, Claude Code + Godot, 5-6 hours of content.



Starting the game

\- My starting point was that I wanted to play a game like Valheim on my phone, and I couldn't find one that scratched the itch, so I started making it myself. I wrote a detailed plan and kept the implementation very basic, just to test the core gameplay. The result was a surprisingly playable proof of concept. I only used Claude Code at this point (with Godot using C#).

\- I quickly realised anyone would get lost in a game like this, so I made an in-game tutorial and got my SO to play it in front of me with no comments from me. It was an eye opener on several points. For example, it was way too hard, and some goals were very confusing (she couldn't work out how to get some items).

\- I kept working on the game, improving it and playing it. With AI, this process was significantly faster, so I could keep the momentum going. The further it went, the more I felt it needed a more polished fighting system. Long story short, I started taking inspiration from other popular games, including Zelda, and added that to the game.



Getting somewhere

\- I felt like I really had something at this point. A simplified Valheim cross Zelda for mobile seemed appealing. As I kept working on the game, I added more friends and family as playtesters. The feedback was very positive (they recruited other playtesters themselves, and one of my playtesters spent 9 hours on it!), but with very clear details needing improvement (usually around goals / player guidance).

\- I really enjoyed researching the lore (ancient Gaul) and creating enemies and bosses based on it. I used ChatGPT images to iterate on ideas from reference images.

\- At this stage, I got more sophisticated creating assets with Blender MCP. Animation can be difficult, but I found that telling Claude to use a video as a reference works pretty well.



Lead up to publishing on Google Play

\- I got a professional playtester to play my game. The feedback was excellent and made me rework some core gameplay elements. It's only with their feedback that I undertood my whole tutorial / goal system was not fit for purpose, so I replaced the whole system with a quest system with sub goals. Again, I felt using AI was amazing here, as I could quickly research how other games do it, then plan something with my own take and implement failry quickly.

\- Finally, I expanded the game a fair bit to make it a complete experience and I reworked all sounds with ElevenLabs. With around 5-6 hours of playtime, I thought it was enough to release publicly.

\- As you may know, new Google Play apps need 12 testers. I already had more than that, but they weren't playing strictly every day, so I used a tester exchange app to get more. A couple of weeks later (which is today), the game is now live!



I'm a SWE so there are some basic I use when using Claude Code that worked well for the project:

\- A handoff doc (.md file) with the decisions, the architecture and the open items. Clear plans for each features, updated as they build.

\- Automated playtest mode that plays through the game (96 steps) and takes screenshots as well as unit testing for key features.

\- As much as possible content is data. Items, recipes, enemies, biomes and quests are all JSON files.

\- For assets I always try to start with an existing asset so that I can re-use some of the rigging and general shape. I then feed that into Claude + Blender, working out the look first then the animations.



It feels like an achievement to finish and publish a game (although there is much more I want to do with it). 

Note: Video is a bit choppy for some reasons but the game runs smoothly on any modern phone.



Right now the game is completely free and offline. Feel free to give it a try here: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nospoonstudio.samonios](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nospoonstudio.samonios)

replies.author: nospoon99

C# has a lot more solid production code available online, so AI models are better at creating code with it than GDscript. Also it's quite fast, when generating the map speed does count.

As for Json it's simple and works well. I haven't hit any problem using it.

comments.author: yaxir
comments.body:
>I'm a SWE so there are some basic I use when using Claude Code that worked well for the project:

>\- A handoff doc (.md file) with the decisions, the architecture and the open items. Clear plans for each features, updated as they build.

>\- Automated playtest mode that plays through the game (96 steps) and takes screenshots as well as unit testing for key features.

>\- As much as possible content is data. Items, recipes, enemies, biomes and quests are all JSON files.

>\- For assets I always try to start with an existing asset so that I can re-use some of the rigging and general shape. I then feed that into Claude + Blender, working out the look first then the animations.

>It feels like an achievement to finish and publish a game (although there is much more I want to do with it).



Your point about reusing existing assets and rigs is especially relevant to what I am trying to do. I am making a 2D action game with AI-generated character designs, and considering editable 3D characters rendered into sprites. I have no artist or animator.

Could you walk through one enemy or character as an example?

1. Where did the starting model and rig come from, and how did you adapt its appearance to your ChatGPT concept without breaking the rig?

2. Which Blender MCP integration did you use, and how did you give Claude the animation reference: the video directly, selected frames, or extracted motion data?

3. What still required your own manual Blender work, particularly joint deformation, clothing and hands holding weapons? Could you create later actions from the same saved character?

Even a short before/after example or a reusable script would help me understand what is realistically achievable.
